{"id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104.2","title":"catch-up 2: per-provider entitlement ranges (the participation-window MUST)","description":"docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §8, and the part the note says implementers will get wrong.

The hub must record, per room and per provider, the sequence ranges during which that provider had a participant. A catch-up answer is bounded by them: nothing from before its first participant joined, nothing from after its last left. Otherwise catch-up becomes a retroactive read of a room the provider was removed from, which is a worse hole than the one being closed.

This is the main NEW STATE the design needs. The hub already tracks the participant list and the Commits that change it; what it does not keep is the mapping from those changes to §4's sequences. Design that mapping before writing the serving code.

Tests, each showing a wrong provider is refused, as AGENTS.md requires of an authorization boundary: a provider that joined at sequence 500 is refused 1 to 499; one that left at 900 is refused 901 onward; one that was never a participant is refused everything; one that left and rejoined gets both of its ranges and not the gap between them.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T01:12:49.295632973Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T01:12:49.295632973Z","labels":["wg"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104.2","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-23T01:12:49.33191953Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"},{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104.2","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104.1","type":"blocks","created_at":"2026-11-23T01:13:15.899456919Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
new_value: {"notes":"Keyword downgraded: decision mimid-1wgh.107 (Mark, 2026-11-22) makes the participation-window bound a SHOULD, not a MUST -- a provider holds no MLS group keys, so a loose bound costs bandwidth and leaks metadata but never message content, and no peer can detect the violation. mimid still follows it. The practical effect on this bead is that the entitlement ranges are an efficiency and metadata-hygiene feature, not an authorization boundary that gates deploying .3: a conservative default (serve nothing before the provider's first join) is enough to start, and precision at the edges can be refined without an interop risk."}
